questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes policy iteration from value iteration?

options.A: Policy iteration evaluates a policy then improves it; value iteration repeatedly applies a Bellman optimality backup.
options.B: Policy iteration requires a known model; value iteration learns only from sampled episodes without a model.
options.C: Policy iteration maximizes only immediate rewards; value iteration also considers discounted future rewards.
options.D: Policy iteration updates values once per policy; value iteration fully evaluates each policy before changing it.

questions.explanation: Policy iteration alternates policy evaluation and greedy improvement. Value iteration combines these through repeated max-over-actions Bellman backups without fully evaluating a policy each time.

questions.text: In a discounted tabular MDP, two actions have equal expected return in one state. Policy iteration keeps switching between them despite unchanged values. Which change directly addresses this instability?

options.A: Increase the discount factor until one action becomes strictly better.
options.B: Stop evaluation when the average value change is small instead of the maximum.
options.C: Choose randomly between tied actions at every improvement step.
options.D: Use a fixed action ordering to break ties consistently at every improvement step.

questions.explanation: A stable tie-break prevents equally good actions from alternating across improvement steps, allowing the policy-stability check to succeed without changing the objective.

questions.text: A value-iteration loop starts with V(s)=0. One nonterminal state has two actions: action left gives reward -1 then enters a terminal with V=0; action right gives reward -1 then returns to the same state. With γ=0.9, what is V(s) after one Bellman optimality backup?

options.A: 0, because both successor values start at zero.
options.B: -0.9, because the reward is discounted on the first step.
options.C: -1, because each action gives -1 and its successor currently has value zero.
options.D: -1.9, because the backup adds the rewards from both available actions.

questions.explanation: The backup computes max_a [r + γ V(next)]. Both actions yield -1 + 0.9×0 = -1 on the first sweep.
